verdict.rationale: HumanLayer's own docs describe per-task worktrees, a task model that groups multiple sessions, and running its stack on remote workers. Together these imply work can be spread across isolated tasks and hosts, but no document explicitly states that many agent tasks run concurrently. Every tutorial and the automation guide describes running 'one' task or session at a time. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of concurrent or parallel task execution, concurrency limits or scaling guidance, a fleet or batch launch view, and independent or hands-on corroboration of throughput at scale.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can run many agent tasks concurrently to scale delivery throughput

citations.quote: Use workspace config to create task worktrees for one or more repositories.
run the HumanLayer stack on your workstation or remote workers
Tasks group agent sessions, artifacts, and worktrees in one workspace that you can collaborate on with your whole team.
